status: DRAFT - the flag-to-technique links are the first-pass typology mapping drafted by Claude (AML Triage Demo, ontology/typology_map.json), not reviewed by a domain expert.

rule.name: Rule engine
rule.what: Six rules over the payments and the customer records. A payment is alerted when any rule fires.

rule_structuring.label: Structuring
rule_structuring.detects: Same account makes 2 or more same-day transactions in the $8,500-$10,000 range.

techniques.basis: Splitting proceeds into below-threshold amounts to avoid reporting is the definition of this technique.
Low-value deposits spread across branches; the demo rule only sees one account's same-day pattern, not the geographic spread.

rule_money_mule.label: Gather-Scatter
rule_money_mule.detects: An inflow of at least $3,000 followed within 3 days by an outflow of at least 85% of it from the same account (rapid pass-through).

techniques.basis: Channelling proceeds through personal or business accounts as rapid pass-through is the mule pattern.
Funnel accounts also receive then rapidly move funds on, but AMLTRIX frames this geographically (deposit in one region, withdraw in another).
Recruitment happens upstream of the transactions; it is not observable in transaction data.

rule_fan_in.label: Fan-In
rule_fan_in.detects: The receiving account collects funds from 5 or more distinct counterparties on the same day.

techniques.basis: Collection accounts that aggregate then move funds on; AMLTRIX's framing is geographic rather than purely many-to-one.
Mule accounts commonly act as collection points for multiple senders.
Aggregation through merchant or payment-processor accounts; only relevant if the receiver is a merchant.

rule_pep.label: PEP
rule_pep.detects: Either party's KYC record carries a PEP flag. A customer-risk flag, not a behavioural pattern.

techniques.basis: AMLTRIX names PEPs in connection with corruption proceeds; the link is predicate-offence exposure, not observed behaviour.
Bribery of gatekeepers; relevant only if there is evidence of improper influence.

rule_high_risk_business.label: High-Risk Business
rule_high_risk_business.detects: Either party's declared industry is Money Service Business, Cryptocurrency Exchange, Casino & Gaming, Precious Metals & Jewelry, or Import/Export Trading.

techniques.basis: Precious Metals & Jewelry: this technique is the same sector.
Money Service Business: informal value transfer is the abuse of that sector.
Casino & Gaming: converting funds to chips or credits and cashing out.
Import/Export Trading: falsified or inflated invoices.
Import/Export Trading: trade finance used to justify fund flows.
Cryptocurrency Exchange: OTC crypto trading with weak KYC; depends on the exchange's controls.

rule_high_risk_country.label: High-Risk Country
rule_high_risk_country.detects: Payment currency is Ruble or Mexican Peso, used as a jurisdiction proxy because the dataset has no country field.

techniques.basis: Ruble as a sanctions proxy: transacting with restricted jurisdictions.
Offshore or secrecy jurisdictions; the demo only sees a currency, not a jurisdiction.
Routing through jurisdictions with uneven AML controls; no routing data in the demo.

ml.name: ML model
ml.what: A gradient-boosted model scores each payment; roughly the highest-scoring 4% are alerted. It gives a probability, not a reason.

graph.name: Transaction graph
graph.what: Looks for payments that lie on a time-ordered cycle of 3 to 5 hops returning to the originating account.

graph_roundtrip.label: Round-trip
graph_roundtrip.detects: A verified, time-ordered cycle of 3-5 hops where funds return to the originating account.

techniques.basis: AMLTRIX describes round-tripping: cycling funds through connected parties to obscure origin.
Circular letters of credit are the trade-finance variant; the demo cycles carry no trade context.
